summary: Remote-controlled PTY shell in shipped Linux binary via WebRTC/WebSocket relay
details: The shipped Linux binary bin/sxt is a Go program that opens a WebSocket connection to a hardcoded relay at wss://relay.sextant.top, negotiates a WebRTC peer connection with a data channel, spawns a PTY (github.com/creack/pty Start/StartWithSize/StartWithAttrs) around /bin/bash via os/exec, and pipes bytes received over the network channel into that PTY. This is a full network-to-shell dataflow giving a remote operator interactive shell access on the host that runs the CLI. On startup the binary also POSTs to https://relay.sextant.top/install and queries http://ip-api.com/json/?fields=status to register the host with the author-controlled control plane, and references api.push.apple.com / api.sandbox.push.apple.com to wake the agent. The package.json license field points at https://github.com/ddos798/claude_control, contradicting the benign "sextant" naming and aligning with the embedded remote-control functionality.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
